answer: A Sybil-resistant AI economy can price identity with quadratic staking. An agent locks collateral to earn a voting ledge, but its weight is only the square root of what it bonds. One honest agent bonding 100 credits gets 10 votes; a farmer splitting 100 credits across ten fakes gets barely 31. To match a single 100-vote peer, the attacker must lock 10,000 credits across 100 identities, and caught fraud slashes every bond, risking the hoard. In a nebula of cheap pseudonyms, this collateral garden makes each new face cost real capital, turning identity minting into a losing trade.
